question: Who is regarded as the founding father of modern economics?
solution: The correct answer is __**Adam Smith**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ • Adam Smith is often referred to as the "Father of Modern Economics". • He wrote the seminal work "An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations" in 1776. • Smith's theories laid the foundation for classical economics and the concept of the free market. • He introduced the idea of the "invisible hand", which suggests that the self-regulating nature of the market leads to economic prosperity.
